name: The Roças of Sao Tome and Principe: Colonial Agricultural System and Forced Migration
description: Six former Portuguese plantations, called roças, are spread across the islands of São Tomé and Príncipe off West Africa. Each was a self-contained estate, with coffee and cocoa fields, processing buildings, workers' housing and social facilities laid out in a planned way. From the late 1800s, they relied on forced labour brought in after slavery ended, and they now show how this system worked.
